stemBlocks.value: Think first: Four terms with no factor common to all of them — that is the signal to group them in pairs.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p092-q01 from workbook page 92.

solutionSteps.instruction: Take the common factor out of each pair.

contentBlocks.value: 3 from the first pair, 2a from the second

strategyBlocks.value: Pair the terms so that each pair has a common factor, take that factor out, then take out the bracket the two pairs share.

whyThisWorks.value: Grouping works because factorising each pair reveals the same bracket in both terms, and that bracket can then be taken out exactly like a common number or letter. Expanding the answer returns the four original terms, which is the check.

commonErrors.misconception: Taking out only 2 instead of 2a from 2ax + 2ay, so the two brackets do not match.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Taking out only 2 instead of 2a from 2ax + 2ay, so the two brackets do not match.

commonErrors.misconception: Stopping at 3(x + y) + 2a(x + y), which is a sum and not yet a product.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Stopping at 3(x + y) + 2a(x + y), which is a sum and not yet a product.

commonErrors.misconception: Pairing terms that share nothing, such as 3x with 2ay.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Pairing terms that share nothing, such as 3x with 2ay.

examTip.value: After grouping, the two brackets must be identical — if they are not, re-pair the terms before going on.
